facts.text: A physics-based model computes outcomes from the laws of nature, while a data-driven model learns typical outcomes from recorded examples.
facts.quote: A physics-based model computes what happens from the laws of nature, while a data-driven model learns what usually happens from recorded examples.

facts.text: Physics-based, signal-level sensor models trace light or radio-energy rays through a scene and model materials, attenuation and electronics.
facts.quote: Physics-based, signal-level models trace rays of light or radio energy through the scene and model materials, attenuation and electronics

facts.text: Physics-based, signal-level sensor models respond causally to a new machine or sensor position and therefore can extrapolate.
facts.quote: they respond causally to a new machine or sensor position, so they can extrapolate

facts.text: Physics-based, signal-level sensor models require supplier internals and measured material data and are costly.
facts.quote: but they need supplier internals and measured material data and are costly.

facts.text: Simplified or phenomenological sensor models start from perfect geometry and add noise, missed detections and attenuation laws.
facts.quote: Simplified or phenomenological models start from perfect geometry and add noise, missed detections and attenuation laws

facts.text: Simplified or phenomenological sensor models are very fast and suitable for massive sweeps once their validity domain is known.
facts.quote: they are very fast and suit massive sweeps once their validity domain is known

facts.text: Simplified or phenomenological sensor models cannot produce effects that nobody encoded.
facts.quote: but they cannot produce effects nobody encoded.

facts.text: Sensor models learned from data, including neural rendering and generative networks, reproduce real recordings well but are tied to their training data and weak at new viewpoints.
facts.quote: Models learned from data (neural rendering, generative networks) reproduce real recordings well but are tied to their training data and weak at new viewpoints.

facts.text: A cited study compared an ideal model, a data-driven model and a ray-tracing radar model; the ideal model produced deceptively realistic tracking output but had "the highest overall gap" when raw output was compared.
facts.quote: One cited study compared an ideal model, a data-driven model and a ray-tracing radar model; the ideal model gave a deceptively realistic tracking output but "the highest overall gap" once its raw output was compared

facts.text: Experts disagree about whether physics-based or data-driven models are superior; the booklet concludes that neither has an unconditional advantage.
facts.quote: Experts disagree on which side wins, and the booklet's reading is that neither has an unconditional advantage [Chapter 5].

facts.text: The collision-mitigation validation program must test many machine models with different sensor heights, a situation where learned models fail and physics-based models can extrapolate.
facts.quote: The program must test many machine models with different sensor heights, which is exactly where learned models fail and physics-based models can extrapolate

facts.text: Physics-based models need job-site material data, but the booklet found that nobody has measured the needed data yet.
facts.quote: but physics-based models need job-site material data that, the booklet found, nobody has measured yet [Chapters 5, 6].
